REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JUNE 8, 2017 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT HELD ON JUNE 8, 2017,
IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Associate Pastor Mark Lohman, New Life Community
  Church.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was given by the VolunTeens Munachismo Okoli and
  Bryan Lee.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Proclamations were presented to:

  Sumati Tilve (100th Birthday Celebration).

  Cerritos High School Dance/Drill and All Male Dance Team (National
  Championship).

5B.  Consideration of appointments to Commissions and Committees (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Pulido, to appoint
  Councilmember Yokoyama’s appointees, Michelle Guerrero and Hyun Kim, to the Let
  Freedom Ring Committee for a two-year term effective June 8, 2017 through March 31,
  2019 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding the community survey.

  Chris Craig announced upcoming events sponsored by Assemblymember Garcia.
  He submitted publicity flyers for the record.

  Martin Grossman spoke regarding the proposed City budget.

  Jay Gray spoke regarding the community survey, searchable .pdf files, and the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.

  Gail Grossman spoke regarding community priorities.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by
  one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of May
  25, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the City
  Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of May 25, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated June 8, 2017
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated June 8, 2017 in the amount of
  $9,403,745.61 (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7C.  Approval of the Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending April 30, 2017
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Treasurer’s Reports for the period ending April 30, 2017 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR
  AGENCY). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration by the City Council of the City of Cerritos of all options
  relating to the potential creation of the Cerritos-Astor museum/learning center
  project, which may include potential use or disposition of the collection and the
  properties located at 12880 Moore Street and 12616 183rd Street (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Budget Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments.

  John Watts spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  John Dawson spoke in support of the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Martin Grossman spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Mel Cortez spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Carol Horn spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Leah Nass spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Jennifer Pilapil spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Gail Grossman spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Jay Gray spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  C.W. Vanderlinden spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum. He
  submitted a document for the record entitled, "Sequoia Ave. Tree Trim Oct. 20
  2003."

  Sam Desai spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  James Yee spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Anantha Ramachandran spoke in opposition to the Cerritos Astor museum.

  Noting there were no further members of the public who elected to speak, the Mayor
  closed public comments and the public hearing.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to disposition the
  Cerritos Astor museum collection via auction or private sale upon
  recommendation of a consultant and lease the 183rd Street and Moore Street
  properties. Leasing of the 183rd Street building would take place upon the
  completion of insurance settlement related improvements (COUNCIL). The motion
  carried (3 - 2) as follows:

  AYES:  Solanki, Yokoyama, Hu
  NOES:  Edwards, Pulido
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  June 8, 2017
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 4 of 5

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of a contract for generator and related hardware
  services, RFP No. 1303-17 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Vince Brar, Senior Assistant City Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Pulido, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $102,512.00 for Generator and Related
  Hardware Services, RFP No. 1303-17 to Global Power Group, Inc. and reject
  the other proposals; and
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any contract-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of budget priorities community survey (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Laurie Kajiwara, Public Information Manager.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to declare the
  budget priorities community survey closed and direct staff to remove it from the
  website (COUNCIL). The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or
  Federal Legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.

  None.

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Edwards, Solanki, and Yokoyama,
  Mayor Pro Tem Pulido, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council did not recess into Closed Session and Items 12A and 12B were

13.  Adjournment

  The meeting was adjourned at 10:25 p.m. in memory of Robert “Bob” Steres,
  father of City Attorney Mark Steres, and Eliya “Ellie” Dumapias Obillo.
